title: SSE interrupt tolerance and tool-call boundary protocol
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Clients using the Redwood streaming API can experience mid-response disconnects (network flaps, browser tab suspend, mobile backgrounding). When disconnects occur during a response that includes function/tool calls or structured JSON output, naive reconnection can cause duplicated function calls, malformed JSON shapes, or lost semantic boundaries. This ticket defines and implements an SSE-side protocol layer to improve interrupt tolerance while preserving deterministic tool-call semantics and structured output boundaries across reconnects. Scope: protocol handshake changes (resume token + affinity window), chunk framing hints to mark semantic boundaries, backward-compatible enrichment headers for older clients, SDK parsing helpers, server-side checkpointing and lightweight idempotency markers for function/tool-call handoff, and end-to-end tests and benchmarks.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can reconnect and resume streams without producing duplicate tool/function calls for idempotent operations in 99.9% of simulated disconnects
Structured outputs (JSONL and explicit JSON frames) can be reassembled safely across reconnects without generating invalid JSON or losing trailing fields
New SSE framing (semantic-hint envelope) degrades gracefully for legacy clients: old clients still get a readable stream, new clients can resume with tokens
Server emits resume token in initial handshake and periodically in chunk envelope; SDKs expose a single-line resume API and automatically rehydrate partial outputs
Performance overhead of added metadata & checkpointing is <5% p50 latency for 2k token sequences in dedicated infra benchmarks
decisions: Use an opt-in resume token advertised in the SSE initial event (X-Resume-Token) and inside periodic 'meta' chunks to limit token churn
Introduce a lightweight semantic-chunk header (semantic_hint) per chunk: values: 'soft-boundary', 'hard-boundary', 'toolcall-start', 'toolcall-end', 'jsonl-line'

Tool/function-call invocation will require a small idempotency marker (tool_call_id) emitted by server before the tool-call chunk; on reconnect, clients will ACK latest tool_call_id and server will avoid re-invoking non-replayed tool calls
Adopt a 250ms chunk-affinity window to tolerate micro-reconnects; during affinity window server will hold minimal state to reconcile late segments
Backward compatibility: if client doesn't send Accept-Resume header, server will not emit sensitive ids and will fall back to existing streaming behavior

E2E tests: flaky disconnect harness, JSON reassembly fuzzing, tool-call replay simulation (SRE + QA)

implementation_notes: Meta chunks will be emitted every 2s or every 256 tokens whichever comes first; meta chunk contains last-ack tool_call_id and resume token hashed with sliding-window salt
semantic_hint 'soft-boundary' signals that a chunk boundary is a good place to resume but does not guarantee atomicity; 'hard-boundary' must be used around JSON blocks and at toolcall-end

On toolcall-start server emits tool_call_id and a small snapshot of arguments (arg-hash). If the client reconnects and resumes from the same resume token, server checks for a persisted completion marker for that tool_call_id before deciding to re-run invocation

We will not persist full function-call side-effects; instead we rely on idempotency markers and the customer's backend function implementations to be idempotent for side-effects. Add docs/guidance for customers to make long-running tool endpoints idempotent
For legacy compatibility, server will fallback to an older event type 'data' without semantic_hint when the client omits Accept-Resume header
To reduce token overhead, resume token is a short stable identifier (base62) referencing server-side checkpoint object; checkpoint TTL is 6 hours by default
risks: Complexity of maintaining ephemeral checkpoints at scale could increase memory pressure for high-concurrency workloads

Customers relying on side-effectful tool endpoints may still observe duplicates if their tool endpoints are not idempotent; we can mitigate via guidance and optional adaptive hold-until-confirmation mode
Misinterpretation of semantic_hint by third-party proxies could strip headers or reorder chunks leading to malformed structured output; will add proxy compatibility tests
rollout_plan: Beta: enable on a subset of runtime nodes behind feature flag; invite 5 high-traffic customers to opt-in
SDK release: coordinated JS/Python SDK updates with automatic resume helpers and opt-in flag
Canary: enable as default for newly created hosted API keys after 2 weeks of beta without critical issues
Full rollout: enable for all keys with a default TTL for resume checkpoints; provide migration & rollback playbook
qa_notes: Simulate 10k disconnects with randomized timing (0-10s) across sequences with toolcalls and assert no duplicate tool invocations in idempotent-mode
Fuzz JSON streaming output across reconnects to ensure parsers do not produce invalid JSON or throw
Verify legacy client still receives continuous stream without resume tokens when Accept-Resume not set
Measure overhead with meta chunks enabled under p95 load on dedicated GPU nodes
